Add arrowheads that point at locations

Source: R/arrows.R
add_arrows.Rd

Adds arrowheads that mark locations in the images, such as a vesicle or a contact site. An arrowhead belongs to an image, not to a channel: it is drawn at the same place in every panel of that image, in each channel and in merges and overlays. Crops and zooms show it wherever its tip falls inside their region.

Usage

add_arrows(montage, at, size = 2, units = c("rel", "px"), color = NULL)

Arguments

montage

A tidymontage() object.

at

Positions of the arrow tips: a numeric vector c(x, y) for one arrowhead on every image, or a data frame with columns x and y and columns of the images tibble to match on, e.g. condition or filepath. A data frame can have several rows per image; images without a matching row get no arrowheads.

size

Length of an arrowhead in mm.

units

Units of at: "rel" (relative, 0-1) or "px".

color

Colour of the arrowheads. NULL (the default) picks white or black, whichever contrasts with the panel.

Value

The montage with the arrow step added.

Details

Each arrowhead is a filled triangle whose tip is at the given position. All arrowheads point in the same direction, from the lower right to the upper left at 45 degrees, and have the same size in every panel. By default they contrast with the panel: white on dark panels, black on light ones.

Positions are given like the centers of add_crop(): relative to the full image by default (0 = left or top edge, 1 = right or bottom edge), or with units = "px" as pixel coordinates of the full image, counted from 0 as in ImageJ / Fiji. Calling add_arrows() again adds more arrowheads.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
arrows <- tibble::tribble(
  ~condition, ~x,   ~y,
  "ctrl",     0.48, 0.42,
  "ctrl",     0.55, 0.38,
  "ko",       0.41, 0.50
)
montage |> add_arrows(arrows)
} # }
